newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn planting most advanced since 1985.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn planting most advanced since 1985.

text.p: Corn planting was brisk in Ohio during the week ended Sunday and reached 71 percent complete, three weeks ahead of average and the most advanced since 1985, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
About three percent had emerged versus none a year ago and the one percent average.
"Many farmers are finished planting corn and have turned their attention to planting soybeans," the report said.
Oats were 93 percent planted and 54 percent of the planted acreage had emerged. The crop was rated nine percent excellent, 49 good, 37 fair, and five poor.

Winter wheat was 44 percent jointed versus 39 a year ago and the 32 average. The crop was rated 11 percent excellent, 42 good, 33 fair, 11 poor and three very poor, a slight improvement from the previous week.
Pasture conditions were rated 50 percent good to excellent, 36 fair, 11 poor and three very poor.
